newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bullion ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Indian bullion ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) closed 20 rupees lower at 7,530 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,550 rupees on demand resistance from industrial consumers at higher level. Silver was up by 105 rupees per kg last week.

** Gold 24-carat closed 5 rupees lower at 4,870 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,875 rupees on the back of profit-taking at the higher level. Gold was up by 95 rupees per 10 gramme last week.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 56,900 rupees per piece after opening at the steady level of 57,000 rupees.
Silver (.999) closed 20 rupees lower at 7,530 rupees per kg amid sluggish physical buying, dealer said.

The market opened 20 rupees lower at 7,530 rupees against the previous close of 7,550 rupees as industrial buying petered out at the higher level while a subdued trend in world markets prompted profit-taking.
"Silver prices during the day hovered around opening level and closed at the opening level," one broker said.
Silver was up by 70 rupees per kg on Saturday and by 105 rupees per kg last week.
Gold 24 carat on the other hand closed 5 rupees lower at 4,870 rupees per 10 gramme as light profit-taking capped early gains towards the close, dealers said.

Gold opened 5 rupees higher at 4,880 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,875 rupees but later on demand resistance and fresh arrivals dragged prices downward towards the close. Gold was up 25 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday and 95 rupees last week.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees at 56,900 rupees per piece. They were up by 300 rupees per piece on Saturday and by 1,100 rupees per piece during last week.
Overall market sentiments was subdued at the close of the session.
